title: Protecting Patients' Interests and Supporting the Medical Community
what_it_is: Protecting Patients' Interests and Supporting the Medical Community

sections.label: Orthopaedic surgeon fined for consent
sections.summary: An orthopaedic surgeon, Dr Lim Lian Arn, was alleged to have failed to obtain informed consent and was fined $100,000, the maximum under the Medical Registration Act.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The first decision was in respect of an orthopaedic surgeon, Dr Lim Lian Arn, who was alleged to have failed to obtain informed consent from his patient before performing a procedure, and was fined $100,000, the maximum fine permitted under the Medical Registration Act.

sections.label: Psychiatrist released sensitive medical information
sections.summary: A psychiatrist, Dr Soo Shuenn Chiang, was alleged to have failed to verify a family member's identity before releasing a memorandum with sensitive medical information.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The second decision concerned a psychiatrist, Dr Soo Shuenn Chiang, who was alleged to have failed to take appropriate steps to verify the identity of his patient's family member before releasing a memorandum containing her sensitive medical information to the family member.

sections.label: DT decisions undermine confidence
sections.summary: The two DT decisions and uncertainty over doctors' obligations risk undermining public and medical profession confidence.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The two DT decisions, as well as the uncertainty surrounding the current law on doctors' obligations, risk undermining the confidence of both the public and the medical profession.

sections.label: Four concerns from the cases
sections.summary: Four concerns arise: informed consent, routing of radiological reports, fairness of convictions and sentences, and remedying SMC DT disciplinary process weaknesses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Four specific concerns arise from these cases: one, what constitutes proper informed consent; two, whether radiological reports with adverse findings should be returned to the doctors or teams who had ordered them, or should they be routed to another specialist department for follow-up; three, whether the convictions and sentences are fair and reasonable, and reflect practice realities on the ground; and four, how to remedy the weaknesses of the SMC DT disciplinary process.

sections.label: SMC annual complaint average
sections.summary: The SMC receives an average of 170 complaints annually.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Annually, the SMC receives an average of 170 complaints.

sections.label: Long case hearing times
sections.summary: Cases take too long, with the CC taking up to two years and a DT up to another two years, occasionally longer.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: It currently takes too long for a case to be heard.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: It takes up to two years and occasionally longer for the CC to reach a conclusion and, if a DT is convened, up to another two years to conclude the case, and occasionally even longer.

sections.label: SMC disciplinary process review
sections.summary: The Ministry will review the SMC disciplinary process and has appointed a workgroup to completely review the SMC's complaints and disciplinary processes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: My Ministry will review the SMC disciplinary process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We must seek to achieve clearer and more consistent outcomes faster, and which both the public and the medical community will have confidence in.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I have appointed a workgroup comprising doctors, legal professionals and other persons with relevant expertise to completely review the SMC's complaints and disciplinary processes.

sections.label: Workgroup recommendations deadline
sections.summary: The workgroup's recommendations are expected by the end of the year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The workgroup’s recommendations are expected by the end of the year.

sections.label: Dr Lim Lian Arn fine
sections.summary: Dr Lim Lian Arn was fined $100,000 for failing to take informed consent for a procedure, bringing the issue to the fore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The recent case where Dr Lim Lian Arn was fined $100,000 for failing to take informed consent for a procedure has brought this issue to the fore.

sections.label: Workgroup to study informed consent
sections.summary: The workgroup reviewing the SMC Disciplinary Processes will also review and study the legal and practical applications of taking informed consent.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: First, the workgroup that is reviewing the SMC Disciplinary Processes will also review and study the legal and practical applications of taking informed consent.

sections.label: Legally binding clinical practice guidance
sections.summary: MOH intends to issue legally binding clinical practice guidance in specific areas to provide additional practice guidance to the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Second, to provide additional practice guidance to the community, MOH intends to issue legally binding clinical practice guidance in specific areas.

sections.label: Guidance on next-of-kin requests
sections.summary: Guidance can be issued on how healthcare institutions and professionals handle requests for assistance from patients' next-of-kin and verify their identities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, guidance can also be issued on how healthcare institutions and professionals should handle requests for assistance from patients’ next-of-kin and, in particular, verify the identities of the next-of-kin, a question raised by Dr Chia Shi-Lu and Dr Lim Wee Kiak.

sections.label: Radiologists' adverse report responsibilities
sections.summary: Radiologists were not expected to bear primary care responsibility for adverse reports, which were routed to ordering doctors; the Ministry will study legislation on doctors' and institutions' responsibilities and report routing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The position hitherto has been that radiologists are not expected to bear any primary care responsibility when there are adverse reports, and that such reports should be routed back to the doctor(s) who ordered the tests.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: My Ministry will also study the existing legislation, with a view to setting out in legislation what should be the legal and ethical responsibilities of the doctors involved and the institutions, and how reports with adverse findings should be routed.

sections.label: Support for disciplinary tribunals
sections.summary: Current disciplinary tribunal cases must continue to avoid delay, while SMC and MOH will provide greater support and streamline the process for smoother, more considered decisions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: The current cases under the DT must continue, otherwise there will be further undue delay.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: However, SMC and MOH will look into how we can provide greater support to the DT and the process and to streamline wherever possible so that the process will be smoother and the judgement and the decision of the DTs will be more considered.

sections.label: SMC handling urgent complaints
sections.summary: When the SMC receives a complaint, it will also look at the nature of the complaint and deal more urgently with those having elements of urgency.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Yes, in fact, the SMC, when they receive a complaint, they will also look at the nature of the complaint.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Some of the complaints have certain elements of urgency and they will deal with them more urgently.

sections.label: Committee on sentencing guidelines
sections.summary: A committee on sentencing guidelines has been set up and will develop a set of guidelines to help guide disciplinary tribunals in meting out sentences.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As I have mentioned in my speech, we have set up a committee on sentencing guidelines, and the committee will then develop a set of guidelines to help guide DTs in meting out their sentences.
